messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: prod-inference-01 KV cache eviction rate spiked above 10% for 3 consecutive 1m windows (rule: kv_cache_eviction_rate > 0.10 for 3m). Auto-page to #eng-oncall.
Alex: ack, I'm on it. grabbing logs and checking dashboards.
Priya: handing off oncall to Alex — I did an initial restart of the cache worker earlier at 09:12 but evictions climbed back. Context: traffic surge from a couple of high-token batches.
Sam: how bad is customer impact? any 5xxs or only latency?
Maria: some customers reported user-facing latency spikes, p95 up ~400-600ms on generation endpoints. No increase in 500s in the last 5m but timeouts started creeping in on longer seq requests.
Jordan: stacktrace shows frequent OOM-ish evictions in the LRU layer, but no full OOMs. Eviction logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:24:12Z] evict key kv:session:abc123 size=2.3MB reason=memory_pressure
[2026-03-15T09:24:13Z] cache_hit=false ttl=0
```
looks like prefix caching isn't hitting; hit_rate dropped from 86% -> 52% over 10m.
Alex: OK. immediate mitigation options: 1) raise cache memory limit on prod-inference-01 (risk of node OOM), 2) route heavy long-seq traffic to dedicated pool, 3) enable aggressive prefix caching (safer), 4) fallback to smaller model variant for affected routes. Thoughts?
Priya: I'd prefer enabling prefix caching + short-term routing rules. Raising memory is risky during peak.
Sam: agree. enable prefix caching now and put a temporary throttling rule on large-token requests (burst limit 3 per min).
Alex: doing: toggling prefix caching config (kv_cache.prefix_enabled=true) and adding rate limit rule for seq>1024. Patching in 30s.
SRE-Ops: confirm config change pushed to prod-inference-01 pool at 09:27. Watching hit_rate.
Jordan: after change, hit_rate climbed to ~72% in 2m, evictions dropped to 3% over 5m window. latency p95 improving.
Maria: customer ops — we should notify affected customers about transient degradation and mitigation steps. I'll draft a note.
IncidentBot: Incident status: mitigation in progress. Pages silenced for the eviction alert for 30m while we monitor.
Alex: quick runbook note for post-incident: needs alert tuning and observability gaps: - eviction-rate alert too noisy (threshold currently 10%) - need separate alerts for sustained hit-rate drop and sudden eviction spikes - lack of hit-rate per-prefix dashboard - no eviction-by-reason metric on alerting.
Sam: propose the following alert changes: 1) new alert: kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.70 for 5m -> severity P1 if P95 latency impact > 250ms, otherwise P2. 2) eviction spike alert: kv_cache_eviction_rate_instant > 0.12 for 1m -> P1. 3) add anomaly detector for sustained degraded hit-rate over 30m.
Jordan: also recommend creating a dashboard tile: "KV Cache – Hit rate by prefix" showing top 20 prefixes, and an eviction waterfall: eviction_count by reason (memory_pressure, ttl_expiry, manual).
Priya: note for oncall: add a synthetic check that runs a small prefix workload every 60s to keep cold-start misses observable. If synthetic hit_rate < 0.65 for 3m, page SRE team.
Alex: created quick Grafana panel (temp) and alerted infra to create a durable dashboard: query used: `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[1m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests[1m])) by (prefix)` and `sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (reason)` — will paste into ticket.
SRE-Ops: filed infra ticket INF-4473 to: a) add dashboard, b) create alerts, c) add eviction reason label to existing metric. Assigned to Jordan and Sam. ETA 48h.
Maria: add product/ops item: evaluate whether certain customer prefixes should be pinned or given reserved cache quota. This drove the eviction cascade.
Sam: quick thresholds we agreed: - hit-rate alert: 70% for 5m -> page P2, escalate to P1 if latency impact > 250ms for 5m. - eviction spike alert: >12% for 1m -> page P1. - eviction-by-reason > 1000/min -> P2.
Alex: post-incident follow-ups: 1) tune alerts per above (owner: Sam) 2) durable dashboard (owner: Jordan) 3) pin high-value prefixes / quota plan (owner: Maria + Product) 4) add synthetic prefix check (owner: Priya) 5) update runbook with safe-memory increase steps (owner: Alex).
Priya: handing back oncall to Maria at 09:50; Alex will monitor until 10:15 during warm handover.
Maria: thanks all. I'll send the customer note and schedule the follow-up postmortem for tomorrow 11:00 with relevant owners.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved -> mitigation stable for 35m, mark incident as mitigated.
Alex: confirm last check: hit_rate steady ~78%, evictions <2% for 20m, p95 latency back to normal baseline. closing loop. :white_check_mark:
